meta.scene_summary: We are busy modularizing the apocalypse while Alphabet burns the budget to find out why the lights went out.

cooking.headline: The Pentagon just tried to ghost Anthropic and the judge said no
cooking.summary: The Pentagon attempted to blacklist Anthropic without following the rules, proving that even the military struggles with basic procurement bureaucracy. It's the ultimate 'I'm not talking to you' move, except the judge just forced them to unblock the contact.
cooking.plain_english: A federal judge ruled that the Department of Defense's decision to blacklist the AI company Anthropic was procedurally invalid.

cooking.headline: The EPA is essentially setting a 'bypass' flag for data center power consumption.
cooking.summary: The EPA just issued guidance making it easier for data centers to ignore standard pollution laws to keep the servers running. It turns out that when your AI model needs a small power plant to finish a training run, the environment gets demoted to a background process.
cooking.plain_english: The Environmental Protection Agency has released new guidelines that allow data centers to bypass certain air pollution regulations to meet their high energy demands.

cooking.headline: Nuclear energy is finally getting the 'microservice' treatment.
cooking.summary: Smaller reactors are finally making nuclear power viable, promising to fix our energy grid instead of just being a legacy monolith. It's comforting to know we might solve the climate crisis just in time to power the massive energy draw of our own AI-generated garbage.
cooking.plain_english: Advancements in small modular reactor technology are making nuclear power a more practical and scalable energy solution.

cooking.headline: GLM-5.3 just dropped and it's actually open
cooking.summary: In an industry where 'open' usually comes with a 50-page legal document and a subscription fee, this model is actually letting you take the keys. It's refreshing to see a model that doesn't treat its own weights like top-secret government clearance.
cooking.plain_english: The developers of the GLM-5.3 artificial intelligence model have released the underlying data and code for public use.

cooking.headline: Htmx 4.0 is here to remind us that JS frameworks are just fancy plumbing
cooking.summary: Htmx 4.0 has arrived to continue its crusade against the modern web's tendency to ship an entire operating system just to render a button. It turns out you don't actually need to re-architect your life every time you want to update a UI element.
cooking.plain_english: The developers of the htmx software library have released a new version that allows web pages to update content without requiring complex JavaScript frameworks.

cooking.headline: Flatpak finally gets the 'adult supervision' budget it deserves
cooking.summary: The Sovereign Tech Agency just dropped €500k to help Flatpak keep the lights on and the dependencies sane. It turns out that building a universal Linux packaging system is actually important, even if it feels like trying to organize a group project where everyone has a different version of the syllabus.
cooking.plain_english: The Sovereign Tech Agency is providing 500,000 euros to support the development and maintenance of the Flatpak software packaging system for Linux.

cooked.headline: Alphabet is discovering that AI is just a very expensive way to burn cash
cooked.summary: Alphabet is watching $700 billion evaporate because their AI bills are starting to look like a mid-life crisis spending spree. It turns out that when you trade your profit margins for GPU clusters, the stock market treats your roadmap like a group project you forgot to finish.
cooked.plain_english: Alphabet's stock price dropped significantly as investors reacted to the high costs associated with maintaining and developing artificial intelligence technology.

cooked.headline: Stripe decides buying PayPal is like trying to upgrade a legacy codebase from 1999
cooked.summary: Stripe walked away from a $50 billion deal for PayPal, proving that sometimes the best way to handle technical debt is to let someone else keep it. It turns out that inheriting a global payment infrastructure is less of a business opportunity and more of a permanent weekend-ruining emergency.
cooked.plain_english: Stripe has officially ended its efforts to acquire the financial technology company PayPal.

cooked.headline: The internet's version of 'I need to see your manager' just nuked a non-profit
cooked.summary: Autistici/Inventati had their domain seized after a US terrorism designation, which is a pretty aggressive way to handle a service that mostly just provides email and hosting. It's the digital equivalent of the FBI raiding a local library because someone checked out a book they didn't like.
cooked.plain_english: The non-profit technology organization Autistici/Inventati lost control of its primary website domain following a designation by the United States government.

cooked.headline: Google Play's AI moderator is hallucinating copyright strikes
cooked.summary: Luanti got kicked off the Play Store because an automated AI bot decided it was violating copyright, which is ironic for an open-source project. It is the digital equivalent of a bouncer refusing you entry because they don't recognize your face, even though your name is on the guest list.
cooked.plain_english: The open-source game Luanti was removed from the Google Play Store due to an automated AI system incorrectly flagging it for copyright infringement.
